title: A NaN's sign survives arithmetic and shows; grouping normalises it
verdict: `nan_kind`: the sign bit is kept by `-x`; `inf - inf` is -NaN on x86-64
description: Spark passes a NaN's bits through: `-x` flips the sign bit of NaN, `x * -1.0` keeps the sign of the NaN operand, `abs` clears it. A NaN that arithmetic creates (`inf - inf`, `inf * 0`, `sqrt(-1)`) has the sign bit set on the probes' x86-64 JVM, as the x86 default NaN does; on aarch64 the default NaN is positive. `CAST(x AS STRING)` prints `NaN` for both. Grouping, joins and `DISTINCT` replace every NaN by the canonical one (spark-nan-equality).
reference: One NaN (`nan_kind: ONE_NAN`). A writer canonicalises NaN where a result's bits are observed (a `CAST` to binary, a Parquet sink).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

notes: `python -m sverify_dev.spark_fuzz --rows 300 --seed 738`: random rows leaning on the fact's edges, each construct run with spark.sql.ansi.enabled on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, and compared with a model of this fact (value, result type, error class). 4800 of 4800 results as the fact says.
nan_sign[0]: 300 rows, `-a`, `abs(a)`, `a * -1.0D`, `b - b`, 4800 of 4800 results as the fact says.
Spark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.12.1, Linux amd64, local[2], session time zone UTC.
